statusText: The CME weekend halt still governs everything: no venue has quoted NQ since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and none will until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, which is about fifteen hours beyond the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail therefore holds at 10% (low), keeping the action EA_ON and the status green - a pathological one-way price path cannot form while nothing is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than observed extension. What separates this hour from the last three is that the wires did move. The IDF confirmed at roughly 08:08 UTC that its overnight strikes on Ansar and the Ali Taher Ridge near Nabatieh were retaliation for a Hezbollah action against Israeli forces inside the southern Lebanon security zone, turning an exchange previously scored as a one-sided strike into a confirmed two-way one; and Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi stated at roughly 05:09 UTC that Tehran has not decided to resume talks with Washington, that the messages passing through Qatar and Pakistan do not amount to negotiations, and that the United States must meet conditions before shipping resumes. Both are escalatory in direction and neither is observable in price, so both are scored where the contract puts them - Stress, which lifts two points to 50% (elevated), not Tail. Confidence stays at 59% (medium-low): every obtainable input was re-verified from primary sources this hour, but a weekend futures halt with no live price path is precisely the case reserved for that band.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (10%) alone. No venue quotes NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint sits just beyond the horizon at the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, and the danger window brackets that reopen together with its first 90 minutes of price discovery - a full weekend of accumulated headlines expresses there as an opening gap, not as intraday structure. Gap risk is genuinely two-way. Pulling one way: a Hormuz closure Tehran says will not lift until its conditions are met, a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports still in force, fifteen ADNOC vessels attacked since February with the two most recent struck on Thursday evening, Bessent's threatened economic isolation with measures due next week, a now-confirmed two-way Lebanon exchange that produced the deadliest toll since the June framework, and Tehran publicly disowning the negotiation track. Pulling the other: the Iran-Oman talks on defining a sea route through the Strait are still running, and Tehran continues to frame reopening as conditional rather than impossible. Crude can reprice before equities are able to, and Friday's weak consumer prints leave a second, unrelated growth-scare channel open into the 19 August FOMC minutes. This is a general market-risk assessment for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and no trade is being placed or recommended.
headline: First new escalation of the weekend lands on two fronts - Israel confirms the Lebanon strikes answered a Hezbollah attack on its troops, and Tehran says it has not decided to resume talks - but with the CME shut until Sunday there is no tape to price it: Tail holds at 10% on EA_ON while Stress firms to 50%.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from primary sources, remains benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, with the session settling mid-range inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide, and no close near either extreme. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range, about 2.3% below the 52-week high of 30,762.20 and far above the 22,841.42 low. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks and repeated extension that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency, pullback depth, failed-retracement counts and proximity to session extremes are all unobservable this hour; that is a structural absence of evidence, not evidence of calm, and it is the single reason Confidence stays medium-low.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close). VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60%, in a 14.18-14.72 day range and near the bottom of its 13.38-35.30 52-week band - the options market priced no stress into the weekend. The latest H.15 constant-maturity yields, for 13 August, are 2Y 4.15%, 10Y 4.63% and 30Y 5.21%: a positively sloped curve with no acute front-end repricing, and no update is due before Monday. Crude is the one asset carrying the geopolitical premium, and it is carrying it clearly - WTI $82.40, +$1.15 or +1.42% on the day, more than +5% on the week, +3.52% on the month and roughly +33% year-over-year. This remains a textbook conflicting-signal set: equity volatility asleep, rates orderly, energy repricing a supply shock. Per the risk definitions, conflicting signals belong in Stress, not Tail, and that is where they are scored.

GEOPOLITICS (new escalation on two threads, neither priceable). Unlike the previous three runs, this hour produced genuinely new timestamped material. First, Lebanon. The IDF said at roughly 08:08 UTC that its overnight strikes were carried out following a Hezbollah action against Israeli forces in the Ali Taher Ridge area inside the security zone where its troops operate, and that it struck Hezbollah infrastructure in two places about fifteen kilometres apart - Ansar, north of Tyre, and the Nabatieh area, including heavy strikes on the Ali Taher Ridge beneath which Hezbollah maintains a major underground facility. Lebanese media put the Ansar toll at seven killed and three wounded, the worst since the June framework arrangements. The previous assessment scored this as a one-sided Israeli strike; the IDF statement makes it a confirmed two-way exchange with a second target set, which is a wider thread than the one already in the book. Second, diplomacy. Foreign Minister Araghchi said at roughly 05:09 UTC that Tehran has not decided to resume talks with the United States, that messages passing through Qatar and Pakistan do not amount to negotiations, and that Washington would have to meet conditions before shipping resumes; he distinguished those from the separate Oman track, which is working on defining a sea route through the Strait. That explicitly disowns the de-escalation path while leaving the routing talks alive. Everything else is unchanged and unresolved: the Persian Gulf Strait Authority maintains the Strait 'remains blocked and will not be reopened until Iran's conditions are accepted'; the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports stands, with the Navy having fired on a Panama-flagged vessel attempting to bypass it; Bessent's 06:05 UTC threat of economic isolation 'like the world has never seen before', with measures due next week, still sits ahead; and ADNOC now counts fifteen of its vessels attacked since the war began on 28 February, the two most recent - a tanker and a bulk carrier struck by an unknown projectile - hit on Thursday evening, an incident already scored and deliberately not double-counted here. Shipping through the Strait remains far below the roughly 120 large vessels a day seen before the war, and the IEA has cut its second-half 2026 global demand estimate by about 550 kb/d on the closure.

MACRO (observed). Friday's U.S. consumer prints both missed sharply: Retail Sales -0.6% month-over-month against +0.1% consensus, Retail Sales ex-autos -0.3% against +0.2%, and preliminary August Michigan sentiment 51.0 against 54.5. Equities absorbed those misses on Friday with two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency - the reason Tail sat at 7-9% through that cash session while Stress built into the low 40s. The soft-consumer channel is a second, independent thread into the 19 August FOMC minutes, unrelated to the Middle East. No U.S. macro release falls inside this 24-hour horizon; the calendar restarts with the NY Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC on Monday 17 August, re-verified against the economic calendar this run.

SCORING (inference). Tail 10% - low band, EA_ON, green. A shut venue cannot produce a pathological price path, and none of the amplifier conditions the contract requires for 25%+ is observable, let alone confirmed. The level is unchanged despite new escalation because the new information is headline flow with no venue to express it, and because the reopen at which it would express falls about fifteen hours beyond the end of this horizon. Stress 50% - elevated, up two points. Two threads widened this hour on primary-source evidence, neither resolved, and Stress is the correct home for escalation that cannot yet be observed in price; letting it decay while the Strait is blocked, a sanctions package is a week out and the Lebanon exchange has turned two-way would misstate the backdrop. Confidence 59% - medium-low. Every obtainable input was obtained and re-verified against primary sources this hour, and the new material was cross-checked before scoring - the Hormuz vessel reports circulating this morning were confirmed to describe Thursday evening's already-scored attacks rather than a fresh incident. The remaining gap is structural, and a weekend futures halt with no live price path is precisely the case the contract reserves the medium-low band for. Dominant mode is mixed: a halted tape overlaid on genuinely conflicting cross-asset signals and two-way geopolitical threads.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-10% throughout. It held 9% through Friday's European session, eased to 7-9% across the U.S. cash session as the sharp Retail Sales and Michigan sentiment misses produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, and printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress described a clear event arc: 25-28% in the quiet Friday morning hours, building to 40-44% through the U.S. cash session as the data landed, then 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. The 06:00 UTC slot lifted to Tail 10% and Stress 48% on the overnight Ansar strike and the UAE's accusation over the ADNOC tanker attacks, and the 07:00 slot held both levels because nothing further had printed by then. Those past opinions are preserved exactly as published and have not been rewritten in light of the new escalation confirmed this hour. Confidence spent the Friday session in the 30s-50s and firmed to 56-59% after midnight as primary-source verification improved. One slot, 20:00 UTC on 14 August, has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 08:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 07:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly fifteen hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is projected flat at 10% for the first twelve slots and ticking to 11% from 20:00 UTC on 15 August as the reopen edges into view; that increment reflects accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to hold at 50% through the European morning, ease at most a point to 49% across the thin Saturday U.S. hours when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, then firm to 50-51% into the late slots as unresolved threads converge on Sunday's price discovery: the Hormuz impasse and Tehran's conditions of sanctions relief, asset unfreezing and an end to the Lebanon and Gaza wars; the standing U.S. naval blockade and the sanctions package Bessent has promised for next week; a Lebanon exchange now confirmed two-way and its bearing on the June framework; Araghchi's statement that Tehran has not decided to resume talks, set against the still-running Oman routing track; and a soft U.S. consumer picture heading into the 19 August FOMC minutes. Confidence drifts down within the medium-low band from 59% to 56% purely as the last live print recedes further into the past. The real checkpoint sits just beyond this horizon: the reopen at roughly 22:00 UTC on 16 August, which the danger window brackets together with its first 90 minutes of trade. Gap risk there is two-way, and the first live tape - not this forecast - is what will decide whether Tail leaves the low band.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour. European Saturday morning, third full day of the CME weekend halt, and the first hour this weekend in which genuinely new escalation printed on two separate threads. The IDF confirmed at roughly 08:08 UTC that the overnight strikes on Ansar and the Ali Taher Ridge answered a Hezbollah action against its forces inside the southern Lebanon security zone, which makes that exchange two-way rather than one-sided; and Araghchi stated at roughly 05:09 UTC that Tehran has not decided to resume talks with Washington. Tail stays at 10% because no venue quotes NQ, so directional efficiency, pullback depth and proximity to extremes remain unobservable - the new information belongs in Stress, which lifts to 50%.

Saturday mid-morning European hours. No venue quoting, no scheduled U.S. release, and historically the thinnest part of the weekend news cycle. Tail holds at 10% on unchanged reasoning; Stress holds at 50% because the two threads that moved this hour - a confirmed two-way Lebanon exchange and Tehran publicly disowning the negotiation track - are unresolved rather than absorbed, and a shut market defers that repricing to Sunday instead of removing it.

European midday. Tail flat at 10%, deep inside the low band, so the action stays EA_ON and the status green. Stress unchanged at 50%. The one live transmission channel remains crude, which closed at $82.40 after a weekly gain above 5% and is the only asset actually pricing the Hormuz closure; equity volatility at a VIX of 14.25 and an orderly 2Y/10Y curve at 4.15%/4.63% are pointed the other way, and that conflict is scored as Stress rather than Tail exactly as the contract requires.

Early U.S. Saturday. Still no tape and no macro. Tail 10%. Stress eases a point to 49% only because this block of hours is where weekend headline flow is empirically lightest - it is a decay in arrival rate, not an improvement in the underlying set. The Strait stays blocked on Tehran's stated conditions, the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports stays in force, and ADNOC's count of fifteen of its vessels attacked since February keeps the shipping channel live.

U.S. Saturday afternoon. Tail 10%, Stress 49%, Confidence steady at 59% in the medium-low band. The forecast deliberately refuses to decay Stress toward trivial levels: Bessent's threat of economic isolation with measures due next week sits ahead of us, the FOMC minutes land on 19 August, and neither is discounted by the absence of a quote screen.

U.S. Saturday evening. Tail 10% and green. Confidence begins its slow drift to 58% as the price evidence ages - the last live print is Friday's 21:00 UTC close and every passing hour widens that gap - while the assessment itself remains fully sourced. Stress 49%. The material checkpoint is still outside this horizon: the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday, where a full weekend of accumulated headlines expresses as a gap rather than as intraday structure.
